## ✨ Highlights

- 🔒 **A reader no longer reads the passwords in haproxy.cfg** (JANUS-2026-006, medium): the configuration comes back to anyone who may not apply one with its `userlist` and `stats auth` passwords, credential headers and `setenv` values masked.
- 🧰 **HAProxy's runtime at a glance**, on the node's HAProxy page and in janusctl: its **stick tables** (and a blocked client let through), the **sessions** in progress (and one ended), the last **requests and responses it refused** with the byte it stopped at, and which map entry or ACL pattern a value matches.
- 🩺 **A connectivity test from the node**: DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP, ping and traceroute, each step timed - "why is this backend down?" answered from where HAProxy stands, with no shell.
- 📦 **A diagnostic bundle**: a node's state and logs in one file to attach to an issue, read with your own permissions, without the node's secrets.

## 🔒 Security

- **Janus itself** (nodes), its own code:
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-006](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.10.18/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-006.json) - A reader could read the passwords in a node's haproxy.cfg.

    `GetConfig` answered the `os:reader` role with haproxy.cfg as it is: `userlist` passwords (`insecure-password` in clear, `password` as a hash that can be cracked offline), `stats auth` passwords, the `Authorization` or API key header a rule adds or a health check sends, the keys an ACL compares a request's header with. Whoever may not apply a configuration - a reader account on the Controller, an `os:reader` janusctl certificate, an API token limited to it - now gets it with those secrets replaced by `<redacted>`, every line in its place, and the SHA-256 of what it got. Operators and admins still read it whole.

    **Besides updating**: if a reader credential given to someone untrusted may have read a node's configuration, change the passwords and keys in it.

## 🧰 HAProxy diagnostics

Three new tabs on a node's HAProxy page, and the same in janusctl ([Stick tables, sessions and errors](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/haproxy-runtime.md)):

- **Stick tables**: each table with its key type and entries used, a table's entries with what it stores - a rate with its period (`http_req_rate /10s`) -, one key or up to four filters (`http_req_rate > 100`). An operator **clears** an entry, the matching ones or the whole table (behind its name typed): a client a rate limit blocked is let through.
- **Sessions**: what HAProxy is processing - a request not answered yet, a TCP connection relayed -, by frontend, backend or client, their age and next timeout. An operator **ends** one: a stuck WebSocket, a client holding a slot.
- **Errors** (operators): the last request and response HAProxy refused as invalid for each proxy - what it answered 400 or 502 "protocol error" for -, the refused byte marked, its buffer and parser state folded below. `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-Api-Key` and `X-Auth-Token` values are masked.
- **Maps & ACLs: test a value** - which entry of a map, or pattern of a file-backed ACL, it matches, with the method the configuration reads it with (`shop.example.org` matches `.example.org` in a `map_dom`).
- A new example, [`examples/haproxy/rate-limit.cfg`](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.10.18/examples/haproxy/rate-limit.cfg): a rate limit with a stick table, checked by the node's own HAProxy.

## 🩺 Connectivity test

**Tools › Connectivity test** on a node's page, `janusctl system probe` on the command line ([Connectivity test](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/connectivity-probe.md)) - operators:

- **dns** (A/AAAA or a type: CNAME, SRV, TXT, MX, NS, PTR - from the node's resolver or a server given), **tcp**, **tls** (the chain, trusted or not against the system's roots or a CA given, version, ALPN, a stapled OCSP response), **http** (status, protocol - HTTP/2 when negotiated -, headers, the body's first KiB, the time to its first byte), **ping** (with the DF bit: an MTU test, the MTU that stopped it), **traceroute** (the routers on the way, named).
- **Connect to** an address of your choosing while the target still gives the SNI and the Host header - one backend server behind a name, or which certificate HAProxy serves for a name on the node itself; **send from** one of the node's addresses - a VRRP virtual address, an anycast address.
- Each step shows as the node takes it. Bounded: 60 s, 20 echo requests, one HTTP request without a body, 4 tests at once per node; each one is an event (`probe.run`) and in the node's audit.

## 📦 Diagnostic bundle

**Tools › Diagnostic bundle**, `janusctl system support` ([Diagnostic bundle](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/diagnostic-bundle.md)):

- One `janus-support-<node>-<time>.tar.gz`: version and image, services, processes, mounts, kernel parameters, the network, HAProxy's state and configuration, the event log - and, as your role allows, each service's logs and the kernel's messages of this boot and the one before, the SELinux denials among them, the audit.
- **Never a secret**: haproxy.cfg masked whoever makes it, every PEM private key cut out, BGP, VRRP and Consul configurations never read. What your role may not read is left out - never asked for - and `MANIFEST.json` says what and why.
- The Controller's audit records each bundle downloaded: logs leave the Controller.

## 🔌 API

- **HAProxyService**: `TableList`, `TableShow`, `SessionList`, `MapLookup`, `ACLLookup` (readers); `TableClear`, `SessionShutdown`, `ErrorsShow` (operators). `GetConfigResponse.redacted` says secrets were masked.
- **SystemService.Probe** (operators): a server stream, each step an event.
- The `haproxy.config.applied` and `haproxy.config.rejected` events name a configuration by the SHA-256 of its masked text - the same as the file's when it holds no secret.

## 🛡️ SELinux

- janusd may use a raw ICMP socket for ping and traceroute - exactly what an enforcing node denied the connectivity test, measured; nothing else was needed.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- **`make qemu-probe-test`**: every kind of connectivity test from an enforcing node against servers on the runner, a reader refused, zero AVC denials.
- `hack/haproxy-runtime-test.sh`, on every HAProxy branch, now also fills, filters and clears a stick table, ends a held session, captures an invalid request carrying credentials, looks up maps and ACLs, and checks a reader's masked configuration.
- `qemu-system-api-test` makes an admin's and a reader's diagnostic bundle on its node.
- 🐛 A HAProxy lifecycle unit test no longer fails under load (two exit events could come in either order).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update. HAProxy is unchanged. The Controller shows a 🟡 medium 🔒 badge for nodes on an older release.
- **The Controller**: update it to get the new tabs and tools. On a node still on an older release, they say to update the node.
- **Readers**: `janusctl haproxy get-config` and the Configuration tab show `<redacted>` where a secret was (janusctl says so on stderr). A script reading the configuration with a reader credential and expecting the secrets needs an operator's.
- **Events**: a script comparing `haproxy.config.applied`'s `sha256` with the file's own hash sees them differ when the configuration holds secrets.
- **janusctl**: new commands only - `haproxy tables`, `table`, `table-clear`, `sessions`, `session-kill`, `errors`, `map-lookup`, `acl-lookup`, `system probe`, `system support`.
- **The Terraform provider**: nothing changed.
